notes:
Summary: Lost to hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS Sagemaker + native infra). Procurement elected single-cloud approach to reduce vendor count and simplify compliance. Team originally engaged for a Dedicated + VPC POC to power customer support and search reranking.

Timeline / Activities:
- 2025-10-05: Initial inbound (product lead) via trial signup. Owner assigned: Maya Chen.
- 2025-11-02: Intro call - scope: chat support agent (multi-tenant), embeddings search for product catalog, reranking for search results. SE Luis joined.
- 2025-11-16: Security questionnaire submitted (see /drive/security/archipelago). Customer requires SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS integration, data residency in us-east-1.
- 2025-12-08: Demo of Redwood Dedicated (latency benchmarks, routing features). Positive; product team: "Excellent perf but procurement nervous about third party."
- 2026-01-10: POC kickoff - committed 2-week POC on dedicated pool with KV caching and prefix cache enabled. Fireflies: ff_2026-01-15_8492.
- 2026-01-28: POC interim review - Redwood shows ~20% lower 99p latency vs their internal inference prototype. Cost model still higher than their forecast if using on-demand.
- 2026-02-10: Procurement & Cloud Architecture joint call. Cloud team presents internal pricing for AWS native endpoints with committed discount model. Fireflies: ff_2026-02-10_9124.
- 2026-02-21: Final procurement decision meeting. Procurement prioritized vendor consolidation and preferred managed endpoints for single-bill and marketplace procurement.

POC findings / technical notes:
- Performance: Redwood Dedicated met latency SLOs in POC (avg p95=80ms for chat flows).
- Reliability: POC stable; autoscaling tests passed.
- Integration: Redwood supports required KMS + VPC; needed minor network egress rules update.
- Cost: TCO analysis favored hyperscaler when factoring in enterprise discounts, reserved capacity, and existing cloud credits.

Why lost to hyperscaler (customer feedback):
- "We want fewer vendors and a single bill — easier for procurement and finance." (VP of Infrastructure)
- Existing enterprise agreement with AWS gives them 30-40% discounts once committed; AWS native endpoints slide into their compliance framework with less external review.
- Security preferred keeping data within the cloud provider's managed control plane rather than a third-party control plane, despite Redwood's VPC/private options.
- Internal champion (Head of AI) left in Jan — no strong advocate remained to push third-party approval.

Sales summary / Lessons learned:
- Technical fit was strong; differentiation (latency, intelligent routing) resonated with product/infra teams.
- Procurement and finance prioritized vendor consolidation and procurement simplicity over best-in-class performance metrics.
- Need to prep stronger procurement playbook for enterprise buyers with existing cloud enterprise agreements (marketplace listing, cost-offset calculators, financing options).
- Consider creating a short TCO workbook that directly models enterprise discounts vs Redwood contract to counter the 'single vendor' argument.

Next actions (internal):
- Close opportunity as lost (recorded 2026-02-28).
- Set 6-9 month re-engagement cadence (target Q4 2026) to re-open if cloud strategy changes or after major procurement renewals.
- Share POC notes with Product team for feature backlog items that might accelerate win probability (marketplace integrations, simplified procurement packaging).

Contact quotes / snippets:
- "We did like the performance and cache model, but procurement insisted on AWS native endpoints for simplicity." — VP Infra
- "If our vendor consolidation policy relaxes, we'd re-evaluate, but right now it's a hard stop." — Procurement Lead

Open artifacts: pricing comparison (archipelago/redwood-vs-aws-2026-01.pdf), security questionnaire with auditor responses.
